newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends marginally lower.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends marginally lower.

text.p: COMEX copper futures ended slightly lower Monday in quiet trade, with activity seen curtailed this week by the New Year holiday Wednesday.
"There was very little going on with the outrights and spreads both little changed," one trader said.
COMEX March copper ended down 0.35 cent at 98.25 cents, after trading in a 99.15-98.10 cent range, which was inside the wide range seen Friday.
The COMEX January/March spread ended little changed at 2.50 cents.
In the past month, both COMEX and LME copper have been drifting back from six month highs, as LME stocks have recovered from six year lows.
A further small rise in LME warehouse copper stocks is expected in Tuesday's data.

Looking out into 1997, "with the 5.3 year cycle low still not due until 1998 or early 1999, we expect continued pressure on the copper market in general," Merrill Lynch technical analyst Tony Wolfskill said.
But "there are some shorter cycle highs due in the February/March time frame that would coincide with a better seasonal upside bias."
